LF89 \| Flat income tax payment, BNC activities \| 2.2% \| ce taux est de 2,2 % \|; LF90 ; LF91 **Crossing a limit once does not end the regime.** Income from 1 January of year N leaves the micro regime only if a limit was exceeded in **both** previous years, N-1 and N-2: "dépassé pendant 2 années consécutives, en N-1 et en N-2". Before that two-year comparison, adjust each short reference year’s turnover proportionally to its actual time of operation/activity as required by CGI arts. 50-0 and 102 ter. Compare the adjusted reference amounts, not automatically the raw cash totals. For a services case, independently established adjusted N-2 turnover EUR 120,000 (actual short-year receipts EUR 60,000) and full-year N-1 turnover EUR 100,000 both exceed EUR 83,600, so the 2026 micro gate fails; using unadjusted EUR 60,000 would give the wrong result. The EUR 120,000 here is a stipulated valid adjusted input, not a universal 365-day computation rule. This reference-year gate is distinct from the micro allowance/minimum and from VAT startup turnover rules.; LF92 ; LF93 The flat payment (versement forfaitaire libératoire) is an option, not the default. Apply the correct option-year/N-2 RFR and share tests above, the eligible micro and micro-social conditions, and the applicable1%/1.7%/2.2% rate to gross qualifying turnover excluding VAT. Tell Urssaf within the actual option/withdrawal timetable. The Service Public page says “before30September”, while the retained DGFiP method expressly permits option or withdrawal by30September for effect the following1January and by the last day of the third month following creation. Use that precise DGFiP deadline, not its dated2024 numerical threshold examples. Declare the turnover annually in the VFL fields even though IR has been paid through Urssaf: the net amount after the statutory allowance still affects RFR, the effective rate on other household income and the pension-saving ceiling. Do not tax that same micro turnover a second time through the ordinary scale. | 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 276 | An employee or pensioner has tax withheld by the payer. A self-employed person, a farmer, and anyone with rental income, alimony or foreign income pays instead by instalments (acomptes) debited by the tax office each month, or every three months where the taxpayer opts with the service des impôts des entreprises by the date in Section 5.6. They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate. | Actual current components: LF323 An employee or pensioner has tax withheld by the payer. A self-employed person, a farmer, and anyone with rental income, alimony or qualifying foreign income within the PAS collection field pays instead by instalments (acomptes) debited by the tax office each month, or every three months where the taxpayer opts with the service des impôts des entreprises by the date in Section 5.6. Foreign income entitled under the actual treaty to a credit equal to the corresponding French tax is excluded from PAS: reporting it on form 2047 does not make it an acompte base. Foreign income with another credit mechanism requires its own collection test, not an automatic exclusion. Source: https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/11247-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IR-PAS-20-20-10-20260407 . They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate. Historical qualification: Original semantic qualification preserved in predecessor_destination; operative successor clauses govern. |

| 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 292 | \| Below EUR 300 \| One debit in September 2026 \| un seul prélèvement en septembre 2026 \| | Actual current components: LF323 An employee or pensioner has tax withheld by the payer. A self-employed person, a farmer, and anyone with rental income, alimony or qualifying foreign income within the PAS collection field pays instead by instalments (acomptes) debited by the tax office each month, or every three months where the taxpayer opts with the service des impôts des entreprises by the date in Section 5.6. Foreign income entitled under the actual treaty to a credit equal to the corresponding French tax is excluded from PAS: reporting it on form 2047 does not make it an acompte base. Foreign income with another credit mechanism requires its own collection test, not an automatic exclusion. Source: https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/11247-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IR-PAS-20-20-10-20260407 . They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate.; LF324 ; LF325 Where no personalised rate exists, a default grid applies to the monthly base. The page below prints it in full in three versions: metropolitan France and abroad, Guadeloupe with La Réunion and Martinique, and Guyane with Mayotte. | 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 336 | ### 6.1 Regime Optimisation (Micro vs Réel) | Actual current components: LF383 ### 6.1 Regime Optimisation (Micro vs Réel) |
| 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 338 | Micro is simpler, not always cheaper. Réel wins when real costs exceed the flat allowance, so compare actual costs against the allowance rate in the abattement table. The option for the déclaration contrôlée is made within the time allowed for filing the return of the year to be taxed that way. Flag for the reviewer to compute both. | Actual current components: LF385 Compare both actual eligible methods using the complete household tax and contribution facts; costs exceeding an allowance do not alone establish that real taxation is better. The BNC declaration-controlled election deadline is the results-return deadline for the year concerned; the BIC option has its separate CGI50-0 timetable and renewal/renunciation conditions. Historical qualification: Corrected automaticcostthreshold advantage: compare eligibleactualhouseholdtax/contributions/electionfacts. |

CGI art. 197 I-4-a limits the reduction to the tax it reduces: stipulated ordinary single-person T = EUR 500 gives raw EUR 670.75, allowed décote EUR 500 and remaining IR EUR 0, not negative EUR 170.75. This nonrefundable reduction is separate from later refundable credits. | 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 404 | Madelin health, disability, provident and pension contributions are deductible from BNC income for a réel filer, within the ceilings of CGI art. 154 bis. Not available to a micro-entrepreneur. This Guide does not print the ceiling formula: flag it for the reviewer. | Actual current components: LF451 CGI154bis covers qualifying BIC as well as BNC real profits. Micro expenses remain covered by the flat allowance, so this is not an additional micro deduction. Establish the actual compulsory contribution or qualifying insurance/PER component, taxpayer/contract conditions and insurer evidence first. Professional-liability insurance is separate from health/provident/pension coverage.; LF452 ; LF453 For the capped optional branches, let P be the applicable annual social-security ceiling and B the statutory professional profit before these same capped contributions/premiums. Include the exempt profits specified by154bis-II, exclude long-term professional gains/losses, and do not reduce B by carried-forward category deficits. For BNC the retained doctrine uses P at1January of the tax year; the cessation/short-period adjustment has its own rule. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. Deduct only qualifying amounts within the applicable ceiling; aggregate the relevant contributor/collaborator amounts and apply the separate partner and paid/engaged timing conditions. Do not deduct the same payment again from global household income, or substitute the household PER ceiling. Check current product/age eligibility and the complete pension/insurance treatment in the named companions; this Guide does not certify a contract from its bank narration alone. Historical qualification: Ordinarypositive154bis ceilings now supplied for qualifying BIC/BNC/nonnegativeprofit; old blanketBNC-only/full deduction corrected; actualproduct/negativeprofitlimits explicit. |
| 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 406 | ### 6.5 Home Office Deduction (Régime Réel) | Actual current components: LF463 ### 6.5 Home Office Deduction (Régime Réel) |
| 62b7639a5a68324a83a96bb0190fff8b7c76f8c5 | 408 | For a réel BNC filer working from home, a share of rent, electricity, internet and heating may be deducted on the floor-area ratio of the office to the whole home. Document it and keep it consistent year to year. | Actual current components: LF465 For real BNC mixed rented premises, divide total eligible rent, including an applicable professional-use surcharge, between actual professional and private use. BOI4659§70 permits the practical ratio of professional floor area to total area, with the taxpayer retaining the calculation/evidence. Do not allocate the entire rent surcharge automatically to business. Utilities and other mixed costs need their actual professional-use basis; this rent rule is not a universal percentage for every bill. Owned business premises, private-property “rent to oneself”, repairs and depreciation have distinct conditions: neither notional rental value nor a mortgage principal payment is an automatic current deduction.; LF466 ; LF467 ; LF468 ; LF469 For the proprietor’s own additional meals in2026, establish that professional work and the actual, not abnormally chosen, distance prevent eating at home; retain proof of the effective expense. The private home-meal value is EUR5.50 TTC and the ordinary excessive-cost boundary is EUR21.40 TTC, so the ordinary additional-cost maximum is EUR15.90. Start from the actual expense and exclude the private component; an amount above21.40 requires the stated exceptional-necessity/nearby-catering justification for a greater deduction. Without proof, no flat deduction is allowed. These2026 values are not asserted as the2025 income-year values. Business/client hospitality follows its own direct-professional-connection and normal-amount rule, rather than automatically applying the proprietor’s personal-meal formula.; LF470 ; LF471 Professional borrowing must also be split: the borrowed capital repayment is not itself a BNC expense; the qualifying professional interest follows its own rule. Professional order/union subscriptions and current professional study/training have direct provisions in BOI4628. Do not infer that every new qualification or retraining programme qualifies: the same source records the2026 removal of the specified sportsperson insertion/conversion deduction. Historical qualification: Actual mixedrentfloorarea method retained, not universalutilitypercentage/owner-notionalrent; ownmeal/interest/training gates sourced. |

Establish the actual compulsory contribution or qualifying insurance/PER component, taxpayer/contract conditions and insurer evidence first. Professional-liability insurance is separate from health/provident/pension coverage.; LF452 ; LF453 For the capped optional branches, let P be the applicable annual social-security ceiling and B the statutory professional profit before these same capped contributions/premiums. Include the exempt profits specified by154bis-II, exclude long-term professional gains/losses, and do not reduce B by carried-forward category deficits. For BNC the retained doctrine uses P at1January of the tax year; the cessation/short-period adjustment has its own rule. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. Deduct only qualifying amounts within the applicable ceiling; aggregate the relevant contributor/collaborator amounts and apply the separate partner and paid/engaged timing conditions. Do not deduct the same payment again from global household income, or substitute the household PER ceiling. Build the household income, divide by the shares, apply the scale, multiply back, then cap the benefit of the extra shares: https://www.service-public.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F1419; LF667 5. Complete the quotient-cap/special-allowance/DOM/décote and separate CEHR/CDHR methods in `fr-personal-income-tax`, with each tax’s actual reference-income and eligibility conditions, before the eligible credit/advance and withholding reconciliation.; LF668 6. Deduct the instalments already taken and settle the balance on the autumn schedule: https://www.impots.gouv.fr/les-modalites-de-la-declaration-de-revenus-en-2026; LF669 7. File form 2042 with 2042-C-PRO by the deadline for the client's département, and a réel filer's result return by its own earlier deadline. LF89 \| Flat income tax payment, BNC activities \| 2.2% \| ce taux est de 2,2 % \|; LF90 ; LF91 **Crossing a limit once does not end the regime.** Income from 1 January of year N leaves the micro regime only if a limit was exceeded in **both** previous years, N-1 and N-2: "dépassé pendant 2 années consécutives, en N-1 et en N-2". Before that two-year comparison, adjust each short reference year’s turnover proportionally to its actual time of operation/activity as required by CGI arts. 50-0 and 102 ter. Compare the adjusted reference amounts, not automatically the raw cash totals. For a services case, independently established adjusted N-2 turnover EUR 120,000 (actual short-year receipts EUR 60,000) and full-year N-1 turnover EUR 100,000 both exceed EUR 83,600, so the 2026 micro gate fails; using unadjusted EUR 60,000 would give the wrong result. The EUR 120,000 here is a stipulated valid adjusted input, not a universal 365-day computation rule. This reference-year gate is distinct from the micro allowance/minimum and from VAT startup turnover rules.; LF92 ; LF93 The flat payment (versement forfaitaire libératoire) is an option, not the default. Apply the correct option-year/N-2 RFR and share tests above, the eligible micro and micro-social conditions, and the applicable1%/1.7%/2.2% rate to gross qualifying turnover excluding VAT. Tell Urssaf within the actual option/withdrawal timetable. The Service Public page says “before30September”, while the retained DGFiP method expressly permits option or withdrawal by30September for effect the following1January and by the last day of the third month following creation. Use that precise DGFiP deadline, not its dated2024 numerical threshold examples. Declare the turnover annually in the VFL fields even though IR has been paid through Urssaf: the net amount after the statutory allowance still affects RFR, the effective rate on other household income and the pension-saving ceiling. Do not tax that same micro turnover a second time through the ordinary scale. Historical qualification: Corrected option-year/N-2 gate:2026usesRFR2024; separate2027RFR2025 and publishedstrict2.5part examples retained. |

LF89 \| Flat income tax payment, BNC activities \| 2.2% \| ce taux est de 2,2 % \|; LF90 ; LF91 **Crossing a limit once does not end the regime.** Income from 1 January of year N leaves the micro regime only if a limit was exceeded in **both** previous years, N-1 and N-2: "dépassé pendant 2 années consécutives, en N-1 et en N-2". Before that two-year comparison, adjust each short reference year’s turnover proportionally to its actual time of operation/activity as required by CGI arts. 50-0 and 102 ter. Compare the adjusted reference amounts, not automatically the raw cash totals. For a services case, independently established adjusted N-2 turnover EUR 120,000 (actual short-year receipts EUR 60,000) and full-year N-1 turnover EUR 100,000 both exceed EUR 83,600, so the 2026 micro gate fails; using unadjusted EUR 60,000 would give the wrong result. Use that precise DGFiP deadline, not its dated2024 numerical threshold examples. | 5f0e5e653d843c034d78e0bd866a5bfb4f5f4e59^ | 162 | \| MUTUELLE SANTÉ / PRÉVOYANCE \| Not a business expense for a micro filer \| Madelin deduction for a réel BNC filer only \| | Actual current components: LF451 CGI154bis covers qualifying BIC as well as BNC real profits. Micro expenses remain covered by the flat allowance, so this is not an additional micro deduction. Establish the actual compulsory contribution or qualifying insurance/PER component, taxpayer/contract conditions and insurer evidence first. Professional-liability insurance is separate from health/provident/pension coverage.; LF452 ; LF453 For the capped optional branches, let P be the applicable annual social-security ceiling and B the statutory professional profit before these same capped contributions/premiums. Include the exempt profits specified by154bis-II, exclude long-term professional gains/losses, and do not reduce B by carried-forward category deficits. For BNC the retained doctrine uses P at1January of the tax year; the cessation/short-period adjustment has its own rule. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. Deduct only qualifying amounts within the applicable ceiling; aggregate the relevant contributor/collaborator amounts and apply the separate partner and paid/engaged timing conditions. Do not deduct the same payment again from global household income, or substitute the household PER ceiling. Check current product/age eligibility and the complete pension/insurance treatment in the named companions; this Guide does not certify a contract from its bank narration alone. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate. | Actual current components: LF323 An employee or pensioner has tax withheld by the payer. A self-employed person, a farmer, and anyone with rental income, alimony or qualifying foreign income within the PAS collection field pays instead by instalments (acomptes) debited by the tax office each month, or every three months where the taxpayer opts with the service des impôts des entreprises by the date in Section 5.6. Foreign income entitled under the actual treaty to a credit equal to the corresponding French tax is excluded from PAS: reporting it on form 2047 does not make it an acompte base. Foreign income with another credit mechanism requires its own collection test, not an automatic exclusion. Source: https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/11247-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IR-PAS-20-20-10-20260407 . They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate. Historical qualification: Original semantic qualification preserved in predecessor_destination; operative successor clauses govern. |

It works on the tax, not on the income, and it fades out: the décote is the fixed amount in the table below, less the share of the gross tax in the table below, so it shrinks to nothing as the gross tax reaches the threshold. | Actual current components: LF402 A small bill is then reduced by the décote. It works on the tax, not on the income, and it fades out: the décote is the fixed amount in the table below, less the share of the gross tax in the table below, so it shrinks to nothing as the gross tax reaches the threshold. For an eligible gross tax T after the prescribed quotient-cap complements and DOM reduction, the décote is `min(T, max(0, K − 45.25% × T))`, with the actual population’s K and threshold below. CGI art. 197 I-4-a limits the reduction to the tax it reduces: stipulated ordinary single-person T = EUR 500 gives raw EUR 670.75, allowed décote EUR 500 and remaining IR EUR 0, not negative EUR 170.75. This nonrefundable reduction is separate from later refundable credits. Source: https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000053542636/2026-05-02 Historical qualification: Original semantic qualification preserved in predecessor_destination; operative successor clauses govern. |

| 5f0e5e653d843c034d78e0bd866a5bfb4f5f4e59^ | 403 | Madelin health, disability, provident and pension contributions are deductible from BNC income for a réel filer, within the ceilings of CGI art. 154 bis. Not available to a micro-entrepreneur. This Guide does not print the ceiling formula: flag it for the reviewer. | Actual current components: LF451 CGI154bis covers qualifying BIC as well as BNC real profits. Micro expenses remain covered by the flat allowance, so this is not an additional micro deduction. Establish the actual compulsory contribution or qualifying insurance/PER component, taxpayer/contract conditions and insurer evidence first. Professional-liability insurance is separate from health/provident/pension coverage.; LF452 ; LF453 For the capped optional branches, let P be the applicable annual social-security ceiling and B the statutory professional profit before these same capped contributions/premiums. Include the exempt profits specified by154bis-II, exclude long-term professional gains/losses, and do not reduce B by carried-forward category deficits. For BNC the retained doctrine uses P at1January of the tax year; the cessation/short-period adjustment has its own rule. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. Deduct only qualifying amounts within the applicable ceiling; aggregate the relevant contributor/collaborator amounts and apply the separate partner and paid/engaged timing conditions. Do not deduct the same payment again from global household income, or substitute the household PER ceiling. Check current product/age eligibility and the complete pension/insurance treatment in the named companions; this Guide does not certify a contract from its bank narration alone. Historical qualification: Ordinarypositive154bis ceilings now supplied for qualifying BIC/BNC/nonnegativeprofit; old blanketBNC-only/full deduction corrected; actualproduct/negativeprofitlimits explicit. |
| 5f0e5e653d843c034d78e0bd866a5bfb4f5f4e59^ | 405 | ### 6.5 Home Office Deduction (Régime Réel) | Actual current components: LF463 ### 6.5 Home Office Deduction (Régime Réel) |
| 5f0e5e653d843c034d78e0bd866a5bfb4f5f4e59^ | 407 | For a réel BNC filer working from home, a share of rent, electricity, internet and heating may be deducted on the floor-area ratio of the office to the whole home. Document it and keep it consistent year to year. | Actual current components: LF465 For real BNC mixed rented premises, divide total eligible rent, including an applicable professional-use surcharge, between actual professional and private use. BOI4659§70 permits the practical ratio of professional floor area to total area, with the taxpayer retaining the calculation/evidence. Do not allocate the entire rent surcharge automatically to business. Utilities and other mixed costs need their actual professional-use basis; this rent rule is not a universal percentage for every bill. Owned business premises, private-property “rent to oneself”, repairs and depreciation have distinct conditions: neither notional rental value nor a mortgage principal payment is an automatic current deduction.; LF466 ; LF467 ; LF468 ; LF469 For the proprietor’s own additional meals in2026, establish that professional work and the actual, not abnormally chosen, distance prevent eating at home; retain proof of the effective expense. The private home-meal value is EUR5.50 TTC and the ordinary excessive-cost boundary is EUR21.40 TTC, so the ordinary additional-cost maximum is EUR15.90. Start from the actual expense and exclude the private component; an amount above21.40 requires the stated exceptional-necessity/nearby-catering justification for a greater deduction. Without proof, no flat deduction is allowed. These2026 values are not asserted as the2025 income-year values. Business/client hospitality follows its own direct-professional-connection and normal-amount rule, rather than automatically applying the proprietor’s personal-meal formula.; LF470 ; LF471 Professional borrowing must also be split: the borrowed capital repayment is not itself a BNC expense; the qualifying professional interest follows its own rule. Professional order/union subscriptions and current professional study/training have direct provisions in BOI4628. Do not infer that every new qualification or retraining programme qualifies: the same source records the2026 removal of the specified sportsperson insertion/conversion deduction. Historical qualification: Actual mixedrentfloorarea method retained, not universalutilitypercentage/owner-notionalrent; ownmeal/interest/training gates sourced. |

LF89 \| Flat income tax payment, BNC activities \| 2.2% \| ce taux est de 2,2 % \|; LF90 ; LF91 **Crossing a limit once does not end the regime.** Income from 1 January of year N leaves the micro regime only if a limit was exceeded in **both** previous years, N-1 and N-2: "dépassé pendant 2 années consécutives, en N-1 et en N-2". Before that two-year comparison, adjust each short reference year’s turnover proportionally to its actual time of operation/activity as required by CGI arts. 50-0 and 102 ter. Compare the adjusted reference amounts, not automatically the raw cash totals. For a services case, independently established adjusted N-2 turnover EUR 120,000 (actual short-year receipts EUR 60,000) and full-year N-1 turnover EUR 100,000 both exceed EUR 83,600, so the 2026 micro gate fails; using unadjusted EUR 60,000 would give the wrong result. The EUR 120,000 here is a stipulated valid adjusted input, not a universal 365-day computation rule. This reference-year gate is distinct from the micro allowance/minimum and from VAT startup turnover rules.; LF92 ; LF93 The flat payment (versement forfaitaire libératoire) is an option, not the default. Apply the correct option-year/N-2 RFR and share tests above, the eligible micro and micro-social conditions, and the applicable1%/1.7%/2.2% rate to gross qualifying turnover excluding VAT. Tell Urssaf within the actual option/withdrawal timetable. The Service Public page says “before30September”, while the retained DGFiP method expressly permits option or withdrawal by30September for effect the following1January and by the last day of the third month following creation. Use that precise DGFiP deadline, not its dated2024 numerical threshold examples. Declare the turnover annually in the VFL fields even though IR has been paid through Urssaf: the net amount after the statutory allowance still affects RFR, the effective rate on other household income and the pension-saving ceiling. Do not tax that same micro turnover a second time through the ordinary scale. Historical qualification: Source-corrected or expanded method; historical wording preserved here, not an additional current allowance. |

Own extra meals have the separate distance, necessity, private-home-meal and excessive-cost conditions described below. \|; LF157 \| FNAC / AMAZON (books/tech) \| Professional materials or asset \| Identify the purchased item, private portion and actual expense-versus-capital treatment; a merchant name is not an automatic current deduction. \|; LF158 \| ADOBE / MICROSOFT / GOOGLE WORKSPACE \| Software subscription/licence or asset \| Identify professional use, contract period and whether the transaction is a current service or capital item. For a real filer, apply the compulsory/optional contribution provisions and the actual CSG/CRDS treatment; do not deduct every item on an Urssaf debit indiscriminately. \|; LF163 \| IMPÔT SUR LE REVENU / PRÉLÈVEMENT À LA SOURCE \| EXCLUDE \| Tax payment, never deductible \|; LF164 \| CFE (COTISATION FONCIÈRE DES ENTREPRISES) \| Professional-tax posting \| Establish the actual CFE and real-regime treatment with `fr-cfe`; a micro filer has no second deduction on top of the allowance. \|; LF165 \| MUTUELLE SANTÉ / PRÉVOYANCE \| No extra micro expense deduction \| For a real filer, test the actual qualifying contract and CGI154bis conditions/limits; this provision covers qualifying BIC as well as BNC. \|; LF166 \| BANQUE FRAIS / FRAIS TENUE DE COMPTE \| Frais bancaires \| Deductible business account charges \|; LF167 \| STRIPE FEE / PAYPAL FEE \| Commissions bancaires \| Deductible payment gateway fees \|; LF168 ; LF169 (Micro-entrepreneurs do NOT deduct actual expenses: the flat allowance covers all of them.) For self-employed: Rate based on prior year income (taux personnalisé) or neutral rate for first year; Monthly debit from bank account; At annual declaration time, actual tax is computed; if PAS exceeded, refund issued. PAS payments are NOT expenses -- they are advance payments of the annual IR. | Actual current components: LF323 An employee or pensioner has tax withheld by the payer. A self-employed person, a farmer, and anyone with rental income, alimony or qualifying foreign income within the PAS collection field pays instead by instalments (acomptes) debited by the tax office each month, or every three months where the taxpayer opts with the service des impôts des entreprises by the date in Section 5.6. Foreign income entitled under the actual treaty to a credit equal to the corresponding French tax is excluded from PAS: reporting it on form 2047 does not make it an acompte base. Foreign income with another credit mechanism requires its own collection test, not an automatic exclusion. Source: https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/11247-PGP.html/identifiant=BOI-IR-PAS-20-20-10-20260407 . They are computed on the income declared the year before, so a business in its first year has no instalment computed from a declared figure; check the espace particulier for what is actually programmed. The personalised rate is recalculated each September from the spring return, and a married or PACS couple taxed jointly gets an individualised rate automatically. It applies only to each spouse's own income; the household's common income stays on the household rate.; LF324 ; LF325 Where no personalised rate exists, a default grid applies to the monthly base. | 11eb01a42 | 351 |   [ ] Madelin deductions applicable (réel BNC only)? | Actual current components: LF451 CGI154bis covers qualifying BIC as well as BNC real profits. Micro expenses remain covered by the flat allowance, so this is not an additional micro deduction. Establish the actual compulsory contribution or qualifying insurance/PER component, taxpayer/contract conditions and insurer evidence first. Professional-liability insurance is separate from health/provident/pension coverage.; LF452 ; LF453 For the capped optional branches, let P be the applicable annual social-security ceiling and B the statutory professional profit before these same capped contributions/premiums. Include the exempt profits specified by154bis-II, exclude long-term professional gains/losses, and do not reduce B by carried-forward category deficits. For BNC the retained doctrine uses P at1January of the tax year; the cessation/short-period adjustment has its own rule. Establish those actual inputs before using a ceiling.; LF454 ; LF455 \| Eligible risk branch \| Ceiling under CGI154bis-II \| Conditions \|; LF456 \| --- \| --- \| --- \|; LF457 \| Retirement and the specified related guarantees \| max[10% × min(B,8P) +15% × max(min(B,8P)−P,0),10% × P] \| Apply the required reduction for the specified exempt employer-plan contributions and the actual qualifying product. \|; LF458 \| Provident cover and the specified guarantee \| min[7% × P +3.75% × B,3% ×8P] \| Apply the actual qualifying guarantee/contract conditions, including health-cover requirements where relevant. \|; LF459 \| Involuntary unemployment and the specified guarantee \| max[1.875% × min(B,8P),2.5% × P] \| This is not ordinary professional-liability insurance. \|; LF460 ; LF461 These expressions describe the ordinary nonnegative-profit ceiling branches, not a blanket deduction for every product named Madelin or PER. Deduct only qualifying amounts within the applicable ceiling; aggregate the relevant contributor/collaborator amounts and apply the separate partner and paid/engaged timing conditions. Do not deduct the same payment again from global household income, or substitute the household PER ceiling. Check current product/age eligibility and the complete pension/insurance treatment in the named companions; this Guide does not certify a contract from its bank narration alone. Historical qualification: Ordinarypositive154bis ceilings now supplied for qualifying BIC/BNC/nonnegativeprofit; old blanketBNC-only/full deduction corrected; actualproduct/negativeprofitlimits explicit. |
